what_was_done: Fixed for the probe the finding named: a brief.md -> src/main.rs symlink spelled through /var (or through a symlinked alias of tmp_path) now gives ('brief', 'spec-product', 'source', 'project'), and test_spelling_through_symlinked_alias_classes_both_forms fails when the realpath(parent) fallback is removed (checked by mutation in a scratch copy). Not fixed in general. The fallback anchors the literal at os.path.realpath(literal.parent), which collapses every directory symlink on the way, not only the spelling of the root. A path through an in-project directory symlink, spelled through an alias of the root, therefore anchors outside the root, _anchored answers None, and only the resolved form is classed. That is the finding's own failure: 'a literal spelled through a symlinked ancestor of the root gets only the resolved form classed'. Probe, portable: src/dirlink -> /etc, file_path <project>/src/dirlink/hosts gives ('source', 'project', 'unclassified', 'outside'), but the same path spelled <alias of tmp_path>/factory-project/src/dirlink/hosts gives ('unclassified', 'outside'). On macOS the same happens for /var/... against /private/var/..., and for /tmp/... against /private/tmp/.... Fix: before the realpath(parent) fallback, walk literal.parents and anchor at the first ancestor whose realpath equals the resolved root: root.joinpath(literal.relative_to(ancestor)). That collapses only the root's spelling and keeps in-project symlinks literal. Keep the current fallback after the walk. Prototyped in a scratch copy: both spellings then give ('source', 'project', 'unclassified', 'outside'), and all 160 tests in tests/hooks pass. Add the alias-spelled src/dirlink/hosts case to test_classes.py.
